top_categories.workout_context: Race-pace efforts that mimic TjejVättern's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before June.

Road-specific control matters at TjejVättern. Practice on mixed terrain: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 62 miles.
When someone attacks on mixed terrain, you have 10 seconds to respond or you're off the back. This builds that response.
62 miles on mixed terrain burns energy faster than the distance suggests. Train the fade resistance now.
TjejVättern's mixed terrain rewards steady threshold power. Surging and recovering costs more watts than just holding.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at TjejVättern. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
2-minute all-out efforts on mixed terrain. Closing gaps, responding to attacks, sprinting for position. Train the burn.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of TjejVättern. Train it until it feels boring.
At TjejVättern, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
Long rides with hard efforts mixed in. Simulates what TjejVättern's mixed terrain actually does to you.
Double-threshold training builds sustained power with less fatigue. More FTP per hour of training.
Smooth pedaling at 62 miles saves muscle. Bad technique at mile 10 is invisible. At mile 80 it's a cramp.

race_overlay.nutrition: Use training to rehearse an eating and drinking plan for TjejVättern's 62 miles. Start early and use products you tolerate. Use the organizer's current resupply plan for final carry decisions.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at TjejVättern rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on mixed terrain to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Race Simulation, Road Specific, and VO2max to prepare you for 62 miles of mixed terrain in Motala, Sweden.
